## How they got there
Paris Saint-Germain won the 2025-26 final by beating Arsenal on penalties after a 1-1 draw, securing their title among 24 knockout teams. Their campaign profile was defined by elite offensive output, with 97% of that season's group-phase teams having fewer attacks per game and 100% recording fewer passes per game. They also maintained a superior goal difference per game compared to 89% of their peers in the league phase.

## Would the model have picked them?
Although the model assigned a 16.1% probability of reaching the final, significantly higher than the 8.3% base rate for a random knockout team, it ranked Paris Saint-Germain fourth among all participants. Because ranks three and four designate a leading contender while only top-two teams are selected by the model, this squad was not picked despite their high probability score. The model's expectation of 1.73 on its stage scale aligns most closely with reaching the semi-finals rather than the final they actually achieved.

## Weak spots
The team's statistical profile shows clear vulnerabilities in long passes (% of passes), where only 8% of that season's teams had a lower rate, and shot accuracy (% on target), which was better than just 56% of their peers. While the model marked down shots per game with a negative contribution because it beat most teams on that stat, Paris Saint-Germain actually ranked in the top 100% for that metric during the group phase. These lower-ranked statistics suggest areas where the team's performance did not align as strongly with historical patterns associated with deep runs.

messages.content: You are a football performance analyst writing for a curious, data-literate reader. Use ONLY the facts provided. Quote every number exactly as it appears in the facts, with the same rounding. Do not introduce players, managers, matches, events, analyses or numbers that are not in the facts. 'Better than this %' figures say how many teams the club beat on a stat, so higher is always better, including for stats marked '(lower is better)', where beating a team means having the lower value. Write them as 'better than X% of teams', never as 'top X%'. SHAP contributions are measured in knockout stages: a positive contribution means the stat pushed the model's expected stage up by that fraction of a round, a negative one pushed it down. A SHAP contribution is the model's view, not a measure of how good the team was at the stat: a team can rank high on a stat the model marked down, so never call a stat a strength or a weakness because of its SHAP sign. Everything here is a statistical association, not a cause: never say a stat or a team's profile drove, powered, propelled, carried, helped, hindered or prevented a result, and do not explain why a stat got its contribution. Write plain markdown without tables.
